title: In silico and in vitro analysis: Unveiling the therapeutic potential of flavonoids against KLF7 in ovarian cancer.
authors: Bhatnagar, Kartik; Shandilay, Swati; Malaisamy, Arun Kumar; Bhavesh, Neel Sarovar; Chaudhary, Sarika
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接、MD模拟和MM/GBSA分析黄酮类化合物与转录因子KLF7的结合，虽涉及TF-DNA相关蛋白但未聚焦DNA互作，方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains a major clinical challenge due to late-stage diagnosis, molecular heterogeneity, and the frequent development of chemoresistance, leading to poor patient outcomes. These challenges underscore the urgent need to identify transcriptional regulators that drive tumor progression and may serve as potential therapeutic targets. Kruppel-like factors (KLFs) are a family of transcription factors involved in regulating cellular proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Among them, Kruppel-like factor 7 (KLF7) has been implicated as a tumor-promoting regulator in multiple malignancies, including OC. METHODS: A full-length structural model of KLF7 obtained from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database was used for structure-based analyses. Molecular docking and virtual screening were conducted to identify flavonoid compounds with high predicted binding affinity toward KLF7. ADMET analysis was performed to evaluate drug-likeness of compounds. The top-ranked compounds were further analyzed using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and MM/GBSA calculations to assess complex stability and binding energetics. In vitro study of the most stable flavonoid with OC cell lines was performed to check the inhibitory efficacy. RESULTS: Hesperidin, and diosmin showed stable interactions with KLF7 and favorable binding energies during MD simulations. In vitro experiments demonstrated dose-dependent effects of hesperidin and diosmin on OC cells, indicating potential antiproliferative activity. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that hesperidin and diosmin may interact with structurally relevant regions of KLF7 and could serve as potential lead compounds for further investigation.
abstract_zh: 引言：卵巢癌（OC）因晚期诊断、分子异质性及频繁出现的化疗耐药性，仍是临床上的重大挑战，导致患者预后不良。这些挑战凸显了识别驱动肿瘤进展并可能作为潜在治疗靶点的转录调节因子的迫切需求。Kruppel样因子（KLFs）是一类参与调控细胞增殖、分化、凋亡及上皮-间质转化（EMT）的转录因子家族。其中，Kruppel样因子7（KLF7）已被认为在多种恶性肿瘤（包括OC）中发挥促肿瘤调节作用。方法：从AlphaFold蛋白质结构数据库获取KLF7的全长结构模型，用于基于结构的分析。通过分子对接和虚拟筛选，识别对KLF7具有高预测结合亲和力的黄酮类化合物。进行ADMET分析以评估化合物的类药性。对排名靠前的化合物进一步采用分子动力学（MD）模拟和MM/GBSA计算，以评估复合物稳定性及结合能量学。对最稳定的黄酮类化合物与OC细胞系进行体外研究，以检验其抑制效果。结果：橙皮苷和地奥司明在MD模拟中与KLF7表现出稳定相互作用及有利的结合能。体外实验显示，橙皮苷和地奥司明对OC细胞具有剂量依赖性效应，表明其具有潜在的抗增殖活性。结论：这些发现提示，橙皮苷和地奥司明可能与KLF7的结构相关区域相互作用，并可作为进一步研究的潜在先导化合物。
